1→# =============================================================================
     2→# Makefile - Custom KN5000 ROM Build System
     3→# =============================================================================
     4→# Build custom ROMs for the Technics KN5000 keyboard.
     5→#
     6→# Targets:
     7→#   make          - Build ROM and create MAME ROM set
     8→#   make build    - Build custom ROM only
     9→#   make romset   - Create complete MAME ROM set with custom program ROM
    10→#   make clean    - Remove build artifacts
    11→#   make test     - Run in MAME emulator
    12→#
    13→# Requirements:
    14→#   - ASL Macro Assembler (asl) and p2bin in ../tools/asl/
    15→#   - MAME unidasm disassembler in ../tools/unidasm
    16→#   - Original KN5000 ROMs in /mnt/shared/kn5000_original_roms/kn5000/
    17→#   - MAME with kn5000 driver (for testing)
    18→# =============================================================================
    19→
    20→# Tool paths (relative to project root)
    21→ASL_PATH := ../../tools/asl
    22→ASL := $(ASL_PATH)/asl
    23→P2BIN := $(ASL_PATH)/p2bin
    24→UNIDASM := ../../tools/unidasm
    25→
    26→# Assembler flags
    27→# -L generates listing file, -olist specifies listing filename
    28→ASL_FLAGS := -w -q -L
    29→
    30→# Build output directory
    31→BUILD_DIR := out
    32→
    33→# Source files
    34→MAIN_SRC := src/main.asm
    35→INCLUDE_DIR := src/includes
    36→
    37→# Shared code from disasm repository
    38→DISASM_REPO := ../../kn5000-roms-disasm
    39→
    40→# Output files
    41→MAIN_ROM := $(BUILD_DIR)/custom_program.rom
    42→MAIN_DISASM := $(BUILD_DIR)/custom_program.disasm
    43→
    44→# ROM size (2MB for program ROM)
    45→ROM_SIZE := 2097152
    46→
    47→# =============================================================================
    48→# MAME ROM Set Configuration
    49→# =============================================================================
    50→# Original ROM location
    51→ORIGINAL_ROMS := /mnt/shared/kn5000_original_roms/kn5000
    52→
    53→# Output ROM set location (MAME-ready)
    54→ROMSET_BASE := /mnt/shared/custom_kn5000_roms/anotherworld
    55→ROMSET_DIR := $(ROMSET_BASE)/kn5000
    56→
    57→# Files to copy from original ROM set (all required for MAME kn5000 driver)
    58→ORIGINAL_ROM_FILES := \
    59→	kn5000_subcpu_boot.ic30 \
    60→	kn5000_subprogram_v142.rom \
    61→	kn5000_table_data_rom_even.ic3 \
    62→	kn5000_table_data_rom_odd.ic1 \
    63→	kn5000_rhythm_data_rom.ic14 \
    64→	kn5000_waveform_rom.ic307 \
    65→	kn5000_custom_data_rom.ic19
    66→
    67→# The program ROM that gets replaced with our custom build
    68→PROGRAM_ROM_NAME := kn5000_v10_program.rom
    69→
    70→# =============================================================================
    71→# Default target - build everything including ROM set
    72→# =============================================================================
    73→.PHONY: all
    74→all: romset
    75→	@echo ""
    76→	@echo "Build complete!"
    77→	@echo "ROM set ready at: $(ROMSET_DIR)/"
    78→	@echo "Test with: make test"
    79→
    80→# =============================================================================
    81→# Build custom ROM only (no ROM set creation)
    82→# =============================================================================
    83→.PHONY: build
    84→build: $(BUILD_DIR) $(MAIN_ROM) $(MAIN_DISASM)
    85→	@echo "Build complete: $(MAIN_ROM)"
    86→	@echo "Symbols used:   $(SYMBOLS_USED)"
    87→	@echo "Symbols unused: $(SYMBOLS_UNUSED)"
    88→	@echo "Disassembly:    $(MAIN_DISASM)"
    89→
    90→# =============================================================================
    91→# Create build directory
    92→# =============================================================================
    93→$(BUILD_DIR):
    94→	mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)
    95→
    96→# =============================================================================
    97→# Build main program ROM
    98→# =============================================================================
    99→# Symbol/listing file output (ASL listing with symbol table)
   100→LISTING_FILE := $(BUILD_DIR)/main.listing
   101→SYMBOLS_USED := $(BUILD_DIR)/symbols.used
   102→SYMBOLS_UNUSED := $(BUILD_DIR)/symbols.unused
   103→
   104→$(BUILD_DIR)/main.p: $(MAIN_SRC) $(wildcard $(INCLUDE_DIR)/*.inc) $(wildcard src/*.asm) | $(BUILD_DIR)
   105→	$(ASL) $(ASL_FLAGS) -olist $(LISTING_FILE) -i $(INCLUDE_DIR) -i src -i $(DISASM_REPO) -i $(DISASM_REPO)/shared $(MAIN_SRC) -o $@
   106→	@# Extract symbol table from listing, split into used and unused
   107→	@grep -E "^[ *]?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]* :" $(LISTING_FILE) | \
   108→		sed 's/ *| */\n/g' | \
   109→		grep -E " :" | \
   110→		grep -v "^$$" | \
   111→		sed 's/^ *//' | \
   112→		grep -v "^\*" | \
   113→		sort > $(SYMBOLS_USED)
   114→	@grep -E "^[ *]?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]* :" $(LISTING_FILE) | \
   115→		sed 's/ *| */\n/g' | \
   116→		grep -E " :" | \
   117→		grep -v "^$$" | \
   118→		sed 's/^ *//' | \
   119→		grep "^\*" | \
   120→		sed 's/^\*//' | \
   121→		sort > $(SYMBOLS_UNUSED)
   122→	@echo "Symbols: $$(wc -l < $(SYMBOLS_USED)) used, $$(wc -l < $(SYMBOLS_UNUSED)) unused"
   123→
   124→$(MAIN_ROM): $(BUILD_DIR)/main.p
   125→	$(P2BIN) $< $@ -l 0xFF
   126→	@# Verify ROM size
   127→	@SIZE=$$(stat -c%s "$@" 2>/dev/null || stat -f%z "$@" 2>/dev/null); \
   128→	if [ "$$SIZE" -lt $(ROM_SIZE) ]; then \
   129→		echo "Padding ROM to $(ROM_SIZE) bytes..."; \
   130→		dd if=/dev/zero bs=1 count=$$(($(ROM_SIZE) - $$SIZE)) 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' '\377' >> $@; \
   131→	fi
   132→	@echo "ROM size: $$(stat -c%s "$@" 2>/dev/null || stat -f%z "$@" 2>/dev/null) bytes"
   133→
   134→# =============================================================================
   135→# Generate reference disassembly using MAME's unidasm
   136→# =============================================================================
   137→$(MAIN_DISASM): $(MAIN_ROM)
   138→	@echo "Generating reference disassembly..."
   139→	$(UNIDASM) $< -arch tlcs900 -basepc 0xE00000 > $@
   140→
   141→# =============================================================================
   142→# Create complete MAME ROM set
   143→# =============================================================================
   144→.PHONY: romset
   145→romset: $(MAIN_ROM)
   146→	@echo "Creating MAME ROM set at $(ROMSET_DIR)/"
   147→	@# Create ROM set directory
   148→	mkdir -p $(ROMSET_DIR)
   149→	@# Copy original ROM files
   150→	@for rom in $(ORIGINAL_ROM_FILES); do \
   151→		if [ -f "$(ORIGINAL_ROMS)/$$rom" ]; then \
   152→			cp "$(ORIGINAL_ROMS)/$$rom" "$(ROMSET_DIR)/"; \
   153→			echo "  Copied: $$rom"; \
   154→		else \
   155→			echo "  WARNING: Missing original ROM: $$rom"; \
   156→		fi; \
   157→	done
   158→	@# Copy our custom ROM as the program ROM
   159→	cp $(MAIN_ROM) $(ROMSET_DIR)/$(PROGRAM_ROM_NAME)
   160→	@echo "  Installed: $(PROGRAM_ROM_NAME) (custom build)"
   161→	@# Show ROM set contents
   162→	@echo ""
   163→	@echo "ROM set contents:"
   164→	@ls -la $(ROMSET_DIR)/
   165→
   166→# =============================================================================
   167→# Clean build artifacts
   168→# =============================================================================
   169→.PHONY: clean
   170→clean:
   171→	rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)
   172→	@echo "Clean complete (ROM set at $(ROMSET_DIR) preserved)"
   173→
   174→# Full clean including ROM set
   175→.PHONY: distclean
   176→distclean: clean
   177→	rm -rf $(ROMSET_BASE)
   178→	@echo "ROM set removed"
   179→
   180→# =============================================================================
   181→# Test in MAME
   182→# =============================================================================
   183→.PHONY: test
   184→test: romset
   185→	@echo ""
   186→	@echo "Running MAME with custom ROM set..."
   187→	@echo "ROM path: $(ROMSET_BASE)"
   188→	@echo ""
   189→	mame kn5000 -rompath $(ROMSET_BASE)
   190→
   191→# Non-interactive test (just verify ROM loads)
   192→.PHONY: test-verify
   193→test-verify: romset
   194→	@echo "Verifying ROM set with MAME..."
   195→	mame kn5000 -rompath $(ROMSET_BASE) -verifyroms
   196→
   197→# =============================================================================
   198→# Development helpers
   199→# =============================================================================
   200→
   201→# Show hex dump of ROM
   202→.PHONY: hexdump
   203→hexdump: $(MAIN_ROM)
   204→	hexdump -C $(MAIN_ROM) | head -100
   205→
   206→# Show reset vector area
   207→.PHONY: showvector
   208→showvector: $(MAIN_ROM)
   209→	@echo "Reset vector area (0xFFFEE0 = offset 0x1FFEE0):"
   210→	hexdump -C $(MAIN_ROM) -s 0x1FFEE0 -n 32
   211→
   212→# Verify assembler is available
   213→.PHONY: check
   214→check:
   215→	@echo "Checking build tools..."
   216→	@if [ -x "$(ASL)" ]; then \
   217→		echo "  ASL: $(ASL)"; \
   218→		$(ASL) -version 2>&1 | head -1 | sed 's/^/    /'; \
   219→	else \
   220→		echo "  ERROR: ASL not found at $(ASL)"; \
   221→		exit 1; \
   222→	fi
   223→	@if [ -x "$(P2BIN)" ]; then \
   224→		echo "  P2BIN: $(P2BIN)"; \
   225→	else \
   226→		echo "  ERROR: P2BIN not found at $(P2BIN)"; \
   227→		exit 1; \
   228→	fi
   229→	@echo ""
   230→	@echo "Checking original ROMs..."
   231→	@if [ -d "$(ORIGINAL_ROMS)" ]; then \
   232→		echo "  Original ROM directory: $(ORIGINAL_ROMS)"; \
   233→		for rom in $(ORIGINAL_ROM_FILES); do \
   234→			if [ -f "$(ORIGINAL_ROMS)/$$rom" ]; then \
   235→				echo "    OK: $$rom"; \
   236→			else \
   237→				echo "    MISSING: $$rom"; \
   238→			fi; \
   239→		done; \
   240→	else \
   241→		echo "  ERROR: Original ROM directory not found: $(ORIGINAL_ROMS)"; \
   242→		exit 1; \
   243→	fi
   244→
   245→# =============================================================================
   246→# Help
   247→# =============================================================================
   248→.PHONY: help
   249→help:
   250→	@echo "KN5000 Custom ROM Build System"
   251→	@echo ""
   252→	@echo "Targets:"
   253→	@echo "  make          - Build ROM and create MAME ROM set (default)"
   254→	@echo "  make build    - Build custom ROM only"
   255→	@echo "  make romset   - Create complete MAME ROM set"
   256→	@echo "  make test     - Run in MAME emulator"
   257→	@echo "  make clean    - Remove build artifacts (preserves ROM set)"
   258→	@echo "  make distclean- Remove everything including ROM set"
   259→	@echo "  make check    - Verify build tools and original ROMs"

   261→	@echo ""

   263→	@echo "  Build:   $(BUILD_DIR)/"

    11→;   - VGA sequencer extended registers
    12→;   - VGA enable and misc output
    13→;   - Standard sequencer registers
    14→;   - Graphics controller registers
    15→;   - CRTC timing registers
    16→;   - Attribute controller (EGA palette)
    17→;   - DAC palette (9 colors: black, white, RGB, CMY, dark blue)
    18→;   - Calls back to extended init

     8→; I/O ports are memory-mapped at VGA_IO_BASE (0x170000).

## Comprehensive Analysis: Merging main.asm and another_world_vm.asm

Based on my thorough exploration of both codebases, here's a detailed analysis for merging them with conditional assembly:

### A) ORG ADDRESSES

| File | ORG Address | Purpose | Size |
|------|-------------|---------|------|
| **main.asm** | 0xE00000 | KN5000 Program ROM base (2MB total) | 2MB (0xE00000-0xFFFFFF) |
| | 0xEF0000 | Code section start (after 960KB padding) | ~64KB |
| | 0xFFFEE0 | Reset vector location (absolute) | 32 bytes |
| | 0xFFFF00 | Interrupt vector table (absolute) | 256 bytes |
| **another_world_vm.asm** | 0x200000 | VM data start (extension board SRAM) | 128KB |
| | 0x280000 | XAPR extension header + code | ~128KB (to 0x2FFFFF) |

**Key Insight**: `main.asm` runs at reset from 0xFFFEE0 (KN5000 main CPU). `another_world_vm.asm` is an extension board ROM that starts at 0x280000 with XAPR header - completely different memory spaces.

---

### B) HARDWARE INIT DIFFERENCES

**main.asm (via boot_hw_init.asm):**
- Watchdog disable (WDMOD, WDCR)
- System clock setup (CLKMOD = 0x04 for 25 MHz)
- Port configuration (P2, P3, P7, PA-PH, PZ) - all data/address bus pins
- Memory controller (MSAR0-5, MAMR0-5) - block address/mask registers
- DRAM initialization with timing (DRAM1REF, DRAM1CRL, DRAM1CRH)
- Chip select configuration (B0CSL-B5CSH)
- Stack pointer setup at 0x001000 (internal RAM)

**another_world_vm.asm:**
- Assumes extension board is already initialized
- No hardware init code at all
- Direct jumps to VM execution
- Runs in extension board memory space (not main CPU ROM)

**Platform-Specific Conflict**: `main.asm` performs full KN5000 initialization. `another_world_vm.asm` assumes hardware is already set up. This can't be conditional within the same ROM - they're for completely different platforms.

---

### C) ENTRY POINT MECHANISMS

**main.asm:**
- Reset vector at 0xFFFEE0 (entry point for CPU reset)
- Jumps to `Reset_Handler` at 0xEF0000
- Sequential boot: hardware init → VGA setup → display graphics → halt
- Uses standard interrupt vector table at 0xFFFF00

**another_world_vm.asm:**
- XAPR extension header at 0x280000 (4-byte magic 'XAPR' + pointer to routine pointers)
- Direct jump to ENTRY label at 0x280000+offset
- VM bytecode execution loop with thread scheduler
- No reset vector (extension board is called by host)

**Critical Difference**: These are incompatible entry point mechanisms for different hardware architectures.

---

### D) RAM/BUFFER LOCATIONS

| Resource | main.asm | another_world_vm.asm | Notes |
|----------|----------|----------------------|-------|
| Stack | 0x001000 | Via XSP register | main.asm uses internal RAM; VM uses explicit stack pointer |
| VRAM | 0x1A0000 | 0x1A0000 | Same! Video display memory |
| Offscreen buffers | 0x280000 (OFFSCREEN_BUFFER_1) | 0x240000-0x270000 (PAGE_BITMAP_0-3) | Different purposes: main.asm for VGA init, VM for game pages |
| Text variables | 0x000200-0x000202 (TEXT_COLOR, ADDR_BUF) | 0x200000+ (VM_VARIABLES, THREADS_DATA) | main.asm uses tiny buffers; VM uses 512KB for game state |
| Current page pointers | N/A | 0x200000+ (CUR_PAGE_PTR_1-3) | VM only |

**Shared Infrastructure**: Both use VRAM at 0x1A0000, so they could theoretically share the same display. But data structures in 0x200000+ will conflict if both execute simultaneously.

---

### E) SHARED INFRASTRUCTURE

**VGA Setup (SHARED):**
- Both include: `vga_constants.asm`, `vga_io.asm`, `vga_init.asm`
- Both use: VGA_IO_BASE (0x170000), VIDEO_RAM_BASE (0x1A0000)
- Both call: `Write_VGA_Register`, `VGA_Setup`, `VGA_SEQUENCER` macros
- **Palette handling differs:**
  - main.asm: `Setup_Palette` uses VGA_DAC_ADDR_WRITE macro, writes 3 colors
  - another_world_vm.asm: `SETUP_PALETTE` directly writes to 0x1703C8/0x1703C9 ports, variable palettes

**Font Data (DIFFERENT):**
- main.asm: `Font_8x8` - 8x8 bitmap font (ASCII 32-127), 1KB
- another_world_vm.asm: `BITMAP_FONT` - `binclude "hardcoded_data/anotherworld_chargen.rom"`, likely 4KB+

**Drawing Routines (COMPLETELY DIFFERENT):**
- main.asm: Pixel-level character drawing (8x8 cells, bit manipulation)
- another_world_vm.asm: Polygon rasterization (fills with step calculations, line drawing)

---

### F) ASL DIRECTIVES

| Directive | main.asm | another_world_vm.asm | Notes |
|-----------|----------|----------------------|-------|
| cpu | 96c141 | 96c141 | Same (TMP94C241F target) |
| page | 0 | 0 | Same (listing page 0) |
| maxmode | on | on | Same (maximum instruction set) |
| org | Multiple: 0xE00000, 0xEF0000, 0xFFFEE0, 0xFFFF00 | Multiple: 0x200000, 0x280000 | Different memory spaces |

**Includes Used:**

**main.asm:**
```
include "sfr_tmp94c241.asm"       ; CPU register definitions
include "vga_constants.asm"       ; VGA port constants
include "tmp94c241.inc"           ; CPU instruction macros
include "local_macros.inc"        ; Custom 24-bit address macros
include "vga_io.asm"              ; VGA I/O routines
include "vga_init.asm"            ; VGA initialization
include "boot_hw_init.asm"        ; Hardware init
include "font_8x8.asm"            ; Font data
```

**another_world_vm.asm:**
```
cpu 96c141, page 0, maxmode on   ; Directives only (no includes shown in file)
; Uses inline bytecode:
binclude "hardcoded_data/anotherworld_chargen.rom"
binclude "hardcoded_data/str_index.rom"
binclude "hardcoded_data/str_data.rom"
binclude "resources/resource-0x18.bin"   ; bytecode
binclude "resources/resource-0x17.bin"   ; palettes
binclude "resources/resource-0x19.bin"   ; video data
binclude "another_world_logo.bin"
binclude "other_bitmap.bin"
```

**Issue**: another_world_vm.asm doesn't include tmp94c241.inc, but it uses many macros from it (LDIRW, EXTS, MULS, DIV, SRAW, DJNZ, LDB, LDW). It appears to rely on the assembler's built-in support or pre-existing definitions.

---

### G) EXACT INCLUDE FILES FOR main.asm

**From Makefile line 105:**
```makefile
$(ASL) $(ASL_FLAGS) -olist $(LISTING_FILE) \
  -i $(INCLUDE_DIR) \
  -i src \
  -i $(DISASM_REPO) \
  -i $(DISASM_REPO)/shared \
  $(MAIN_SRC) -o $@
```

**Include paths searched (in order):**
1. `src/includes/` - Local macros and constants
2. `src/` - Local assembly files
3. `../../kn5000-roms-disasm/` - Disasm repo root (for SFR definitions)
4. `../../kn5000-roms-disasm/shared/` - Shared VGA/boot code

**Files actually included by main.asm:**
1. **sfr_tmp94c241.asm** - CPU SFR definitions (from disasm repo)
2. **vga_constants.asm** - VGA port constants (from disasm/shared)
3. **tmp94c241.inc** - CPU instruction macros (from disasm repo)
4. **local_macros.inc** - Custom macros (from src/includes)
5. **vga_io.asm** - VGA read/write routines (from disasm/shared)
6. **vga_init.asm** - VGA initialization (from disasm/shared)
7. **boot_hw_init.asm** - Hardware init (from src/local copy)
8. **font_8x8.asm** - Font data (from src/local)

---

### H) INSTRUCTIONS/MACROS COMPARISON

**Instructions used by another_world_vm.asm:**

From tmp94c241.inc:
- **LDIRW** (line 252, 819) - Load, Increment, Repeat (16-bit block copy)
- **EXTS** (lines 142, 537, 543, 696, 704, 866, 870, 906, 915-916) - Extend-signed (sign-extend register)
- **MULS** (line 707) - Multiply-signed (32-bit signed multiplication)
- **DIV** (line 698) - Unsigned division
- **SRAW** (lines 390, 399, 416, 424) - Shift-right arithmetic (sign-extending)
- **LDB** (lines 148, 266) - Load byte (8-bit register write)
- **LDW** (lines 267, 279, 280, 592, 593, 618, 624, 864) - Load word (16-bit register write)
- **DJNZ** (lines 150, 314-315, 323-324, 428, 810, 852, 935, 939) - Decrement register, jump if not zero
- **MUL** (lines 190, 389, 398, 415, 423, 581, 723, 733, 756, 766, 919) - Unsigned multiplication

**Instructions used by main.asm:**

From tmp94c241.inc:
- **LDA_XWA_IMM24** (custom in local_macros.inc) - Load 24-bit address
- **CALR** (from disasm tmp94c241.inc) - Call relative
- **EXTZ_XWA** (custom in local_macros.inc) - Zero-extend WA to XWA
- **EXTZ_WA** (from disasm tmp94c241.inc) - Zero-extend A to WA
- Standard register operations (ld, add, inc, dec, sla, srl, bit, etc.)
- No LDIRW, MULS, DIV, SRAW, LDB, LDW, DJNZ - just standard syntax

**Critical Finding**: another_world_vm.asm **must** include tmp94c241.inc or have these macros defined, but they don't appear in the file. This suggests:
1. Either the file is incomplete/won't assemble as-is
2. Or tmp94c241.inc is expected to be included via the Makefile include paths
3. Or the assembler has native support for these instructions (unlikely for a 1995-era CPU)

---

### I) VGA PALETTE SETUP

**main.asm Setup_Palette (lines 318-337):**
```asm
Setup_Palette:
    VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_ADDR_WRITE, COLOR_CYAN    ; Select palette index 2
    VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0                    ; Cyan: R=0
    VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Fh                  ;       G=0Fh
    VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Fh                  ;       B=0Fh

    VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Ah
    VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Ah
    VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Ah
    ; Yellow (index 4, auto-increment)
    VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Fh
    VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Fh
    VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0
    ret
```
- Uses macro: `VGA_WRITE` (defined in vga_init.asm)
- Writes fixed 3 colors (cyan, light gray, yellow) to DAC indices 2-4
- 6-bit RGB format (4-bit per component as stored, shifted to 6-bit)

**another_world_vm.asm SETUP_PALETTE (lines 822-853):**
```asm

    LD BC, 0
    LD XDE, 01703c8h          ; VGA 3C8 port (select palette index)
    LD (XDE), C

    LD XDE, 01703c9h          ; VGA 3C9 port (palette data)

    ADD XHL, XWA
    
PALETTE_LOOP:

    ANDB A, 0Fh
    LD (XDE), A
    INC XHL
    
    LD A, (XHL)               ; Green (4-bit)
    ANDB A, 0Fh
    LD (XDE), A
    
    LD A, (XHL)               ; Blue (4-bit) - shifted right by 4

```
- Direct port writes (0x170000 + 0x3C8/0x3C9)
- Variable palette selection from `INTRO_PALETTES` resource
- 16 colors per palette, with 4-bit RGB components

**Differences:**
1. main.asm: Hardcoded colors, uses VGA macros
2. another_world_vm.asm: Resource-based palettes, direct port I/O
3. Format: Both 4-bit RGB, but another_world_vm.asm has 16 colors per palette vs 3 colors in main.asm

### J) FONT DATA

**main.asm Font_8x8 (src/font_8x8.asm):**
- 8x8 bitmap font

**Conflict Resolution**: These can coexist if:
- Conditional include: `ifdef MAIN_CPU ... include font_8x8.asm ... else binclude "anotherworld_chargen.rom" ... endif`
- Or: Keep both fonts and reference appropriate one based on mode

---

| Component | main.asm (KN5000 Main CPU) | another_world_vm.asm (Extension Board) | Can Share? | Notes |
|-----------|---------------------------|------|-----------|-------|
| ORG addresses | 0xE00000-0xFFFFFF | 0x200000-0x2FFFFF | NO | Completely different memory spaces |
| Reset vector | 0xFFFEE0 | XAPR header | NO | Different entry point mechanisms |
| Hardware init | Full (watchdog, clocks, ports, DRAM) | None | NO | Extension board already initialized |
| Stack pointer | 0x001000 (internal RAM) | Via XSP | YES | Could be same location |
| VRAM | 0x1A0000 | 0x1A0000 | YES | Both can write to same display |
| VGA setup | Via macros (vga_init.asm) | Direct I/O | PARTIAL | Both initialize VGA, different approaches |
| Palette setup | Hardcoded 3 colors | Resource-based 16 colors | PARTIAL | Can coexist, different data |
| Font | font_8x8.asm (768 bytes) | anotherworld_chargen.rom | NO | Different fonts, could conditionally include |
| Game VM | Not present | Full game interpreter | N/A | Different functionality |
| Display routine | Hexdump viewer | Polygon rasterizer | NO | Completely different rendering |

---

## CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL INSIGHT

**These codebases are not meant to merge into a single ROM!**

- **main.asm**: Runs on KN5000 **main CPU** at reset (0xFFFEE0). Initializes hardware and displays content.
- **another_world_vm.asm**: Runs on **extension board** CPU (HDAE5000), called by main CPU via inter-CPU protocol.

**To run Another World on KN5000:**
1. Main CPU (main.asm) initializes KN5000 hardware
2. Main CPU loads game assets into extension board SRAM (0x200000+)
3. Main CPU jumps to extension board code at 0x280000 via XAPR header
4. Extension board VM interprets bytecode and updates VRAM at 0x1A0000
5. Main CPU displays result on screen

**A merged single-ROM approach would:**
- Break the two-CPU architecture
- Duplicate hardware init (waste space)
- Create namespace conflicts (both use 0x1A0000 for different purposes)
- Require significant refactoring

**Recommendation**: If merging is the goal, create a **launcher ROM** structure:
```asm
ifdef KN5000_MAIN
    ; Hardware init, display setup, inter-CPU protocol
    include "boot_hw_init.asm"
    include "vga_init.asm"
    ; ... load and execute extension board code
else ifdef EXTENSION_BOARD
    ; Game VM code
    include "another_world_vm.asm"
endif
```

But this requires a different build approach (separate ROMs for each CPU, not a single merged ROM).

   253→	ret
   254→
   255→; =============================================================================
   256→; Draw_Hex_Byte - Draw one byte as two hex digits plus space gap
   257→; Input: A = byte value, XDE = screen position
   258→; Output: XDE advanced by 24 pixels (3 char widths)
   259→; =============================================================================
   260→Draw_Hex_Byte:
   261→	push WA				; Save original byte
   262→
   263→	; High nibble
   264→	srl 1, A
   265→	srl 1, A
   266→	srl 1, A
   267→	srl 1, A
   268→	CALR Nibble_To_Ascii
   269→	push XDE
   270→	CALR Draw_Char
   271→	pop XDE
   272→	add XDE, 8			; Advance one char width
   273→
   274→	; Low nibble
   275→	pop WA				; Restore original byte
   276→	and A, 0Fh
   277→	CALR Nibble_To_Ascii
   278→	push XDE
   279→	CALR Draw_Char
   280→	pop XDE
   281→	add XDE, 16			; Advance past char + space gap
   282→
   283→	ret
   284→
   285→; =============================================================================
   286→; Draw_Hex_Byte_Tight - Draw one byte as two hex digits (no trailing space)
   287→; Input: A = byte value, XDE = screen position
   288→; Output: XDE advanced by 16 pixels (2 char widths)
   289→; =============================================================================
   290→Draw_Hex_Byte_Tight:
   291→	push WA				; Save original byte
   292→
   293→	; High nibble
   294→	srl 1, A
   295→	srl 1, A
   296→	srl 1, A
   297→	srl 1, A
   298→	CALR Nibble_To_Ascii
   299→	push XDE
   300→	CALR Draw_Char
   301→	pop XDE
   302→	add XDE, 8			; Advance one char width
   303→
   304→	; Low nibble
   305→	pop WA				; Restore original byte
   306→	and A, 0Fh
   307→	CALR Nibble_To_Ascii
   308→	push XDE
   309→	CALR Draw_Char
   310→	pop XDE
   311→	add XDE, 8			; Advance one char width (no space gap)
   312→
   313→	ret
   314→
   315→; =============================================================================
   316→; Setup_Palette - Program VGA DAC entries 2-4 for UI colors
   317→; =============================================================================
   318→Setup_Palette:
   319→	; Start writing at palette index 2 (cyan)
   320→	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_ADDR_WRITE, COLOR_CYAN
   321→
   322→	; Cyan (R=0, G=0Fh, B=0Fh) - index 2
   323→	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0
   324→	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Fh
   325→	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Fh
   326→
   327→	; Light Gray (R=0Ah, G=0Ah, B=0Ah) - auto-increments to index 3
   328→	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Ah
   329→	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Ah
   330→	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Ah
   331→
   332→	; Yellow (R=0Fh, G=0Fh, B=0) - auto-increments to index 4
   333→	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Fh
   334→	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Fh
   335→	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0
   336→
   337→	ret
   338→
   339→; =============================================================================
   340→; Draw_Border - Draw bordered frame with vertical separator
   341→; Box: (35,16) to (284,233), separator at X=88
   342→; =============================================================================
   343→Draw_Border:
   344→	ld A, COLOR_LIGHT_GRAY
   345→
   346→	; Top horizontal line: (35, 16), length 250
   347→	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
   348→	add XDE, 16 * SCREEN_WIDTH + 35
   349→	ld BC, 250
   350→	CALR Draw_Hline
   351→
   352→	; Bottom horizontal line: (35, 233), length 250
   353→	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
   354→	add XDE, 233 * SCREEN_WIDTH + 35
   355→	ld BC, 250
   356→	CALR Draw_Hline
   357→
   358→	; Left vertical line: (35, 16), height 218
   359→	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
   360→	add XDE, 16 * SCREEN_WIDTH + 35
   361→	ld BC, 218
   362→	CALR Draw_Vline
   363→
   364→	; Right vertical line: (284, 16), height 218
   365→	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
   366→	add XDE, 16 * SCREEN_WIDTH + 284
   367→	ld BC, 218
   368→	CALR Draw_Vline
   369→
   370→	; Separator vertical line: (88, 16), height 218
   371→	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
   372→	add XDE, 16 * SCREEN_WIDTH + 88
   373→	ld BC, 218
   374→	CALR Draw_Vline
   375→
   376→	ret
   377→
   378→; =============================================================================
   379→; Draw_Hline - Draw horizontal line
   380→; Input: XDE = start VRAM address, BC = length, A = color
   381→; =============================================================================
   382→Draw_Hline:
   383→	ld (XDE), A
   384→	inc 1, XDE
   385→	dec 1, BC
   386→	or BC, BC
   387→	jr NZ, Draw_Hline
   388→	ret
   389→
   390→; =============================================================================
   391→; Draw_Vline - Draw vertical line
   392→; Input: XDE = start VRAM address, BC = height, A = color
   393→; =============================================================================
   394→Draw_Vline:
   395→	ld (XDE), A
   396→	add XDE, SCREEN_WIDTH
   397→	dec 1, BC
   398→	or BC, BC
   399→	jr NZ, Draw_Vline
   400→	ret
   401→
   402→; =============================================================================
   403→; Nibble_To_Ascii - Convert 0-15 to ASCII '0'-'9' or 'A'-'F'
   404→; Input: A = nibble (0-15)
   405→; Output: A = ASCII character
   406→; =============================================================================
   407→Nibble_To_Ascii:
   408→	cp A, 10
   409→	jr C, .digit
   410→	add A, 'A' - 10
   411→	ret
   412→.digit:
   413→	add A, '0'
   414→	ret
   415→
   416→; =============================================================================
   417→; Draw_String - Draw null-terminated string at screen position   [0xEF0B67]
   418→; Input: XHL = string pointer, XDE = screen position (VRAM address)
   419→; =============================================================================
   420→Draw_String:
   421→.draw_loop:
   422→	ld A, (XHL)
   423→	or A, A			; Check for null terminator
   424→	ret Z
   425→
   426→	push XDE
   427→	push XHL
   428→	CALR Draw_Char		; Draw character at (XDE), char in A
   429→	pop XHL
   430→	pop XDE
   431→
   432→	add XDE, 8		; Move to next character position
   433→	inc 1, XHL
   434→	jr .draw_loop
   435→
   436→; =============================================================================
   437→; Draw_Char - Draw a single 8x8 character                        [0xEF0B7E]
   438→; Input: A = ASCII character, XDE = screen position
   439→; =============================================================================
   440→Draw_Char:
   441→	; Calculate font data offset: (A - 32) * 8
   442→	sub A, 32		; ASCII offset
   443→	EXTZ_WA			; Zero-extend A to WA (clears W)
   444→	EXTZ_XWA		; Zero-extend WA to XWA (clears upper 16 bits)
   445→
   446→	; Multiply by 8 (shift left 3)
   447→	sla 1, WA
   448→	sla 1, WA
   449→	sla 1, WA
   450→
   451→	; Get font data address
   452→	LDA_XHL_IMM24 Font_8x8
   453→	add XHL, XWA
   454→
   455→	; Draw 8 rows
   456→	ld C, 8			; Row counter
   457→
   458→.row_loop:
   459→	ld A, (XHL)		; Get font row bitmap
   460→	push XDE
   461→	push XHL
   462→
   463→	; Draw 8 pixels
   464→	ld B, 8			; Column counter
   465→
   466→.pixel_loop:
   467→	bit 7, A		; Test MSB
   468→	jr Z, .skip_pixel
   469→
   470→	; Draw pixel in current text color
   471→	push WA
   472→	ld A, (TEXT_COLOR)
   473→	ld (XDE), A
   474→	pop WA
   475→
   476→.skip_pixel:
   477→	inc 1, XDE
   478→	sla 1, A		; Shift to next bit
   479→	dec 1, B
   480→	or B, B
   481→	jr NZ, .pixel_loop
   482→
   483→	pop XHL
   484→	pop XDE
   485→
   486→	; Move to next row
   487→	add XDE, SCREEN_WIDTH
   488→	inc 1, XHL
   489→	dec 1, C
   490→	or C, C
   491→	jr NZ, .row_loop
   492→
   493→	ret
   494→
   495→; =============================================================================
   496→; Serial_Init - Initialize SC0 for computer interface (38400)    [0xEF0BC1]
   497→; =============================================================================
   498→Serial_Init:
   499→	ld (SC0MOD), SC0MOD_8N1
   500→	ld (BR0CR), BR0CR_38400
   501→	ld (SC0CR), 000h
   502→	ret
   503→
   504→; =============================================================================
   505→; Send_Serial_Message - Send "It is working!" to serial port     [0xEF0BCB]
   506→; =============================================================================
   507→Send_Serial_Message:
   508→	LDA_XHL_IMM24 Str_ItIsWorking
   509→
   510→.send_loop:
   511→	ld A, (XHL)
   512→	or A, A			; Check for null terminator
   513→	ret Z
   514→
   515→	CALR Serial_Send_Byte
   516→	inc 1, XHL
   517→	jr .send_loop
   518→
   519→; =============================================================================
   520→; Serial_Send_Byte - Send single byte via SC0                    [0xEF0BDD]
   521→; Input: A = byte to send
   522→; =============================================================================
   523→Serial_Send_Byte:
   524→	push BC
   525→	push DE
   526→
   527→	; Wait for TX buffer empty (bit 1 of SC0CR) with timeout
   528→	ld DE, 0FFFFh		; Timeout counter
   529→.wait_tx_empty:
   530→	ld C, (SC0CR)
   531→	bit 1, C
   532→	jr NZ, .tx_ready
   533→	dec 1, DE
   534→	or DE, DE
   535→	jr NZ, .wait_tx_empty
   536→	jr .send_done		; Timeout - skip send
   537→
   538→.tx_ready:
   539→	ld (SC0BUF), A
   540→
   541→.send_done:
   542→	pop DE
   543→	pop BC
   544→	ret
   545→
   546→; =============================================================================
   547→; Data Section
   548→; =============================================================================
   549→Str_Title:
   550→	db "KN5000 hexdump utility", 0
   551→
   552→Str_ItIsWorking:
   553→	db "It is working!", 13, 10, 0
   554→
   555→; =============================================================================
   556→; Font Data
   557→; =============================================================================
   558→	include "font_8x8.asm"
   559→
   560→; =============================================================================
   561→; Reset Handler Location                                         [0xFFFEE0]
   562→; =============================================================================
   563→	org 0FFFEE0h
   564→
   565→Reset_Entry:
   566→	jp Reset_Handler
   567→
   568→; =============================================================================
   569→; Fill gap between reset entry and vector table
   570→; =============================================================================
   571→	org 0FFFEE4h
   572→
   573→	rept 01Ch
   574→	db 0FFh
   575→	endm
   576→
   577→; =============================================================================
   578→; Interrupt Vector Table                                         [0xFFFF00]
   579→; =============================================================================
   580→	org 0FFFF00h
   581→
   582→VECTOR_TABLE:
   583→	dd 00FFFEE0h		; Vector 0: Reset
   584→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 1
   585→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 2
   586→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 3
   587→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 4
   588→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 5
   589→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 6
   590→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 7
   591→
   592→	rept 56

; =============================================================================
; main.asm - Custom KN5000 Boot ROM: Hexdump Utility
; =============================================================================
; A minimal boot ROM for the Technics KN5000 that:
;   1. Initializes essential hardware (watchdog, memory, ports)
;   2. Initializes the VGA display controller
;   3. Displays a hex dump viewer with title, bordered frame, colored
;      address column, and data display of boot code
;   4. Sends "It is working!" to the serial port (computer interface)
;
; Target: TMP94C241F (TLCS-900/H2) @ 25 MHz
; ROM Size: 2MB (0xE00000 - 0xFFFFFF)
; Reset Vector: 0xFFFEE0
;
; Build: make
; Test: Run in MAME kn5000 driver with custom ROM set
;
; This code reuses shared components from ../kn5000-roms-disasm/
; =============================================================================

	cpu 96c141		; TLCS-900/H target
	page 0
	maxmode on

; =============================================================================
; Include shared definitions from kn5000-roms-disasm
; =============================================================================
	include "sfr_tmp94c241.asm"
	include "vga_constants.asm"
	include "tmp94c241.inc"

; Local macros not in the disasm repo
	include "local_macros.inc"

; =============================================================================
; Memory Map Constants
; =============================================================================
STACK_TOP		EQU 001000h	; Stack in internal RAM
OFFSCREEN_BUFFER_1	EQU 280000h	; Offscreen buffer (required by vga_init)

; Screen dimensions
SCREEN_WIDTH		EQU 320
SCREEN_HEIGHT		EQU 240

; Colors (palette indices)
COLOR_BLACK		EQU 0
COLOR_WHITE		EQU 1
COLOR_CYAN		EQU 2		; Address text
COLOR_LIGHT_GRAY	EQU 3		; Borders/separator
COLOR_YELLOW		EQU 4		; Title text
COLOR_DARK_BLUE		EQU 8

; RAM variables (internal RAM, above Extended SFR region at 0x100-0x1FF)
TEXT_COLOR		EQU 000200h	; 1 byte: current drawing color
ADDR_BUF		EQU 000201h	; 3 bytes: address display value (little-endian)

; Serial port constants
SC0MOD_8N1		EQU 069h	; 8-bit, no parity, 1 stop, baud gen
BR0CR_38400		EQU 006h	; 38400 baud

; =============================================================================
; ROM Layout
; =============================================================================
	org 0E00000h		; Program ROM base address

; Fill with 0xFF until code section
	rept 0F0000h		; ~960KB of padding
	db 0FFh
	endm

; =============================================================================
; Code Section (starts at 0xEF0000)
; =============================================================================
	org 0EF0000h

; Jump to Reset_Handler (VGA code is included first for macro definitions)
	jp Reset_Handler

; =============================================================================
; Include shared VGA I/O and initialization routines
; (defines Write_VGA_Register, VGA_Setup, and macros like VGA_SEQUENCER)
; =============================================================================
	include "vga_io.asm"
	include "vga_init.asm"
	ret			; VGA_Setup has no ret (designed for inline use)

; =============================================================================
; Entry Point - Called after hardware reset                      [0xEF09C5]
; =============================================================================
Reset_Handler:
	; =========================================================================
	; Minimal hardware initialization (local, trimmed from original)
	; Initializes: watchdog, clock, ports, memory controller, DRAM
	; =========================================================================
	include "boot_hw_init.asm"

	; Set up stack pointer (after hardware init)
	LDA_XWA_IMM24 STACK_TOP
	ld XSP, XWA

	; Initialize VGA display using shared code
	CALR VGA_Setup

	; The shared VGA_Setup leaves registers set for buffer init:
	;   XWA = OFFSCREEN_BUFFER_1, BC = 0808h, DE = 38400
	; We skip the offscreen buffer stuff and just clear video RAM directly

	; Clear screen to dark blue
	CALR Clear_Screen

	; Set up additional palette colors (cyan, light gray, yellow)
	CALR Setup_Palette

	; Draw hexdump of boot code with UI
	CALR Draw_Hexdump

	; Turn screen on (sequencer clocking mode)
	VGA_SEQUENCER 01h, 001h

	; TODO: Re-enable serial port code after VGA troubleshooting
	; CALR Serial_Init
	; CALR Send_Serial_Message

	; Enter infinite loop
Main_Loop:						; [0xEF0B36]
	halt
	jr Main_Loop

; =============================================================================
; Default_Handler - Default interrupt handler for unused vectors [0xEF0B39]
; =============================================================================
Default_Handler:
	halt
	jr Default_Handler

; =============================================================================
; Clear_Screen - Fill screen with dark blue (color 8)            [0xEF0B3C]
; =============================================================================
Clear_Screen:
	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
	ld XBC, SCREEN_WIDTH * SCREEN_HEIGHT	; 76800 bytes
	ld A, COLOR_DARK_BLUE

.clear_loop:
	ld (XDE), A
	inc 1, XDE
	dec 1, XBC
	or XBC, XBC		; Set Z flag based on full 32-bit value
	jr NZ, .clear_loop

	ret

; =============================================================================
; Draw_Hexdump - Display hex dump with title, border, and address column
; 8 bytes per line, 27 lines = 216 bytes of boot code
; Input: none
; =============================================================================
Draw_Hexdump:
	; --- Draw title (yellow, centered) ---
	ld A, COLOR_YELLOW
	ld (TEXT_COLOR), A
	LDA_XHL_IMM24 Str_Title
	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
	add XDE, 4 * SCREEN_WIDTH + 72	; Y=4, X=72
	CALR Draw_String

	; --- Draw border ---
	CALR Draw_Border

	; --- Initialize address buffer with Reset_Handler address ---
	ld A, Reset_Handler & 0FFh
	ld (ADDR_BUF), A
	ld A, Reset_Handler >> 8 & 0FFh
	ld (ADDR_BUF + 1), A
	ld A, Reset_Handler >> 16 & 0FFh
	ld (ADDR_BUF + 2), A

	; --- Set up for data display ---
	LDA_XHL_IMM24 Reset_Handler	; Source: boot code in ROM
	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
	add XDE, 17 * SCREEN_WIDTH + 36 ; Y=17, X=36 (inside border)

	ld C, 27			; 27 lines

.line_loop:
	push XDE			; Save line start position
	push XHL			; Save source pointer
	push BC				; Save counters

	; --- Draw address in light gray (3 bytes = 6 hex digits, tight) ---
	ld A, COLOR_LIGHT_GRAY
	ld (TEXT_COLOR), A

	; High byte of address (byte 2)
	ld A, (ADDR_BUF + 2)
	push XDE
	CALR Draw_Hex_Byte_Tight
	pop XDE
	add XDE, 16			; Advance past 2 chars

	; Middle byte of address (byte 1)
	ld A, (ADDR_BUF + 1)
	push XDE
	CALR Draw_Hex_Byte_Tight
	pop XDE
	add XDE, 16			; Advance past 2 chars

	; Low byte of address (byte 0)
	ld A, (ADDR_BUF)
	push XDE
	CALR Draw_Hex_Byte_Tight
	pop XDE
	add XDE, 16 + 8		; Advance past 2 chars + separator gap

	; --- Draw 8 data bytes in white ---
	ld A, COLOR_WHITE
	ld (TEXT_COLOR), A
	pop BC				; Restore counters
	pop XHL				; Restore source pointer
	ld B, 8				; 8 bytes per line

.byte_loop:
	push XHL
	push BC
	ld A, (XHL)			; Read byte from ROM
	CALR Draw_Hex_Byte		; Draw "XX " and advance XDE by 24
	pop BC
	pop XHL

	inc 1, XHL			; Next source byte
	dec 1, B
	or B, B
	jr NZ, .byte_loop

	; --- Increment address buffer by 8 ---
	ld A, (ADDR_BUF)
	add A, 8
	ld (ADDR_BUF), A
	ld A, (ADDR_BUF + 1)
	adc A, 0
	ld (ADDR_BUF + 1), A
	ld A, (ADDR_BUF + 2)
	adc A, 0
	ld (ADDR_BUF + 2), A

	; --- Move to next line ---
	pop XDE				; Restore line start
	add XDE, 8 * SCREEN_WIDTH	; Move down one character row (8 pixels)
	dec 1, C
	or C, C
	jr NZ, .line_loop

	ret

; =============================================================================
; Draw_Hex_Byte - Draw one byte as two hex digits plus space gap
; Input: A = byte value, XDE = screen position
; Output: XDE advanced by 24 pixels (3 char widths)
; =============================================================================
Draw_Hex_Byte:
	push WA				; Save original byte

	; High nibble
	srl 1, A
	srl 1, A
	srl 1, A
	srl 1, A
	CALR Nibble_To_Ascii
	push XDE
	CALR Draw_Char
	pop XDE
	add XDE, 8			; Advance one char width

	; Low nibble
	pop WA				; Restore original byte
	and A, 0Fh
	CALR Nibble_To_Ascii
	push XDE
	CALR Draw_Char
	pop XDE
	add XDE, 16			; Advance past char + space gap

	ret

; =============================================================================
; Draw_Hex_Byte_Tight - Draw one byte as two hex digits (no trailing space)
; Input: A = byte value, XDE = screen position
; Output: XDE advanced by 16 pixels (2 char widths)
; =============================================================================
Draw_Hex_Byte_Tight:
	push WA				; Save original byte

	; High nibble
	srl 1, A
	srl 1, A
	srl 1, A
	srl 1, A
	CALR Nibble_To_Ascii
	push XDE
	CALR Draw_Char
	pop XDE
	add XDE, 8			; Advance one char width

	; Low nibble
	pop WA				; Restore original byte
	and A, 0Fh
	CALR Nibble_To_Ascii
	push XDE
	CALR Draw_Char
	pop XDE
	add XDE, 8			; Advance one char width (no space gap)

	ret

; =============================================================================
; Setup_Palette - Program VGA DAC entries 2-4 for UI colors
; =============================================================================
Setup_Palette:
	; Start writing at palette index 2 (cyan)
	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_ADDR_WRITE, COLOR_CYAN

	; Cyan (R=0, G=0Fh, B=0Fh) - index 2
	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0
	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Fh
	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Fh

	; Light Gray (R=0Ah, G=0Ah, B=0Ah) - auto-increments to index 3
	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Ah
	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Ah
	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Ah

	; Yellow (R=0Fh, G=0Fh, B=0) - auto-increments to index 4
	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Fh
	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0Fh
	VGA_WRITE VGA_DAC_DATA, 0

	ret

; =============================================================================
; Draw_Border - Draw bordered frame with vertical separator
; Box: (35,16) to (284,233), separator at X=88
; =============================================================================
Draw_Border:
	ld A, COLOR_LIGHT_GRAY

	; Top horizontal line: (35, 16), length 250
	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
	add XDE, 16 * SCREEN_WIDTH + 35
	ld BC, 250
	CALR Draw_Hline

	; Bottom horizontal line: (35, 233), length 250
	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
	add XDE, 233 * SCREEN_WIDTH + 35
	ld BC, 250
	CALR Draw_Hline

	; Left vertical line: (35, 16), height 218
	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
	add XDE, 16 * SCREEN_WIDTH + 35
	ld BC, 218
	CALR Draw_Vline

	; Right vertical line: (284, 16), height 218
	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
	add XDE, 16 * SCREEN_WIDTH + 284
	ld BC, 218
	CALR Draw_Vline

	; Separator vertical line: (88, 16), height 218
	LDA_XDE_IMM24 VIDEO_RAM_BASE
	add XDE, 16 * SCREEN_WIDTH + 88
	ld BC, 218
	CALR Draw_Vline

	ret

; =============================================================================
; Draw_Hline - Draw horizontal line
; Input: XDE = start VRAM address, BC = length, A = color
; =============================================================================
Draw_Hline:
	ld (XDE), A
	inc 1, XDE
	dec 1, BC
	or BC, BC
	jr NZ, Draw_Hline
	ret

; =============================================================================
; Draw_Vline - Draw vertical line
; Input: XDE = start VRAM address, BC = height, A = color
; =============================================================================
Draw_Vline:
	ld (XDE), A
	add XDE, SCREEN_WIDTH
	dec 1, BC
	or BC, BC
	jr NZ, Draw_Vline
	ret

; =============================================================================
; Nibble_To_Ascii - Convert 0-15 to ASCII '0'-'9' or 'A'-'F'
; Input: A = nibble (0-15)
; Output: A = ASCII character
; =============================================================================
Nibble_To_Ascii:
	cp A, 10
	jr C, .digit
	add A, 'A' - 10
	ret
.digit:
	add A, '0'
	ret

; =============================================================================
; Draw_String - Draw null-terminated string at screen position   [0xEF0B67]
; Input: XHL = string pointer, XDE = screen position (VRAM address)
; =============================================================================
Draw_String:
.draw_loop:
	ld A, (XHL)
	or A, A			; Check for null terminator
	ret Z

	push XDE
	push XHL
	CALR Draw_Char		; Draw character at (XDE), char in A
	pop XHL
	pop XDE

	add XDE, 8		; Move to next character position
	inc 1, XHL
	jr .draw_loop

; =============================================================================
; Draw_Char - Draw a single 8x8 character                        [0xEF0B7E]
; Input: A = ASCII character, XDE = screen position
; =============================================================================
Draw_Char:
	; Calculate font data offset: (A - 32) * 8
	sub A, 32		; ASCII offset
	EXTZ_WA			; Zero-extend A to WA (clears W)
	EXTZ_XWA		; Zero-extend WA to XWA (clears upper 16 bits)

	; Multiply by 8 (shift left 3)
	sla 1, WA
	sla 1, WA
	sla 1, WA

	; Get font data address
	LDA_XHL_IMM24 Font_8x8
	add XHL, XWA

	; Draw 8 rows
	ld C, 8			; Row counter

.row_loop:
	ld A, (XHL)		; Get font row bitmap
	push XDE
	push XHL

	; Draw 8 pixels
	ld B, 8			; Column counter

.pixel_loop:
	bit 7, A		; Test MSB
	jr Z, .skip_pixel

	; Draw pixel in current text color
	push WA
	ld A, (TEXT_COLOR)
	ld (XDE), A
	pop WA

.skip_pixel:
	inc 1, XDE
	sla 1, A		; Shift to next bit
	dec 1, B
	or B, B
	jr NZ, .pixel_loop

	pop XHL
	pop XDE

	; Move to next row
	add XDE, SCREEN_WIDTH
	inc 1, XHL
	dec 1, C
	or C, C
	jr NZ, .row_loop

	ret

; =============================================================================
; Serial_Init - Initialize SC0 for computer interface (38400)    [0xEF0BC1]
; =============================================================================
Serial_Init:
	ld (SC0MOD), SC0MOD_8N1
	ld (BR0CR), BR0CR_38400
	ld (SC0CR), 000h
	ret

; =============================================================================
; Send_Serial_Message - Send "It is working!" to serial port     [0xEF0BCB]
; =============================================================================
Send_Serial_Message:
	LDA_XHL_IMM24 Str_ItIsWorking

.send_loop:
	ld A, (XHL)
	or A, A			; Check for null terminator
	ret Z

	CALR Serial_Send_Byte
	inc 1, XHL
	jr .send_loop

; =============================================================================
; Serial_Send_Byte - Send single byte via SC0                    [0xEF0BDD]
; Input: A = byte to send
; =============================================================================
Serial_Send_Byte:
	push BC
	push DE

	; Wait for TX buffer empty (bit 1 of SC0CR) with timeout
	ld DE, 0FFFFh		; Timeout counter
.wait_tx_empty:
	ld C, (SC0CR)
	bit 1, C
	jr NZ, .tx_ready
	dec 1, DE
	or DE, DE
	jr NZ, .wait_tx_empty
	jr .send_done		; Timeout - skip send

.tx_ready:
	ld (SC0BUF), A

.send_done:
	pop DE
	pop BC
	ret

; =============================================================================
; Data Section
; =============================================================================
Str_Title:
	db "KN5000 hexdump utility", 0

Str_ItIsWorking:
	db "It is working!", 13, 10, 0

; =============================================================================
; Font Data
; =============================================================================
	include "font_8x8.asm"

; =============================================================================
; Reset Handler Location                                         [0xFFFEE0]
; =============================================================================
	org 0FFFEE0h

Reset_Entry:
	jp Reset_Handler

; =============================================================================
; Fill gap between reset entry and vector table
; =============================================================================
	org 0FFFEE4h

	rept 01Ch
	db 0FFh
	endm

; =============================================================================
; Interrupt Vector Table                                         [0xFFFF00]
; =============================================================================
	org 0FFFF00h

VECTOR_TABLE:
	dd 00FFFEE0h		; Vector 0: Reset
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 1
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 2
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 3
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 4
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 5
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 6
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 7

	rept 56
	dd Default_Handler
	endm

; =============================================================================
; End of ROM
; =============================================================================
	end

   384→	LD WA, 0

   393→	LD WA, 0

   396→	LD DE, 0
   397→	LD E, C
   398→	MUL XWA, DE			; *= ZOOM

   401→
   402→	LD B, (XIX)

   405→
   406→	LD XIY, POLYGON_POINTS

   436→fillPolygon:

   438→	; HL: y

   440→
   441→	PUSH BC

   443→	LD B, 0
   444→
   445→	;if (m_polygon.bbox_w == 0 && m_polygon.bbox_h == 1 && m_polygon.numPoints == 4)
   446→	CPW (POLYGON_BBOX_W), 0

   452→	
   453→	;(color, pt.x, pt.y);
   454→	CALL drawPoint

   457→	NOT_A_POINT:
   458→
   459→	PUSH IX
   460→	; int16_t xmin = pt.x - m_polygon.bbox_w / 2;
   461→	LD IX, (POLYGON_BBOX_W)
   462→	SRA 1, IX
   463→	LD (POLYGON_XMIN), DE
   464→	SUB (POLYGON_XMIN), IX

   466→	; int16_t xmax = pt.x + m_polygon.bbox_w / 2;
   467→	LD (POLYGON_XMAX), DE

   480→
   481→
   482→	;if (xmin >= 320 || xmax < 0 || ymin >= 200 || ymax < 0)
   483→	;	return;
   484→	CPW (POLYGON_XMIN), 320
   485→	JP GE, end_of_fillPolygon
   486→	CPW (POLYGON_XMAX), 0
   487→	JP LT, end_of_fillPolygon
   488→	CPW (POLYGON_YMIN), 200
   489→	JP GE, end_of_fillPolygon
   490→	CPW (POLYGON_YMAX), 0
   491→	JP LT, end_of_fillPolygon
   492→
   493→
   494→	LD WA, (POLYGON_YMIN)
   495→	LD (HLINEY), WA
   496→
   497→	LD XIX, POLYGON_POINTS				; i = 0;
   498→	LD XIY, POLYGON_POINTS
   499→	LD XWA, 0
   500→	LD A, (POLYGON_NUM_POINTS)

   504→

   669→calcStep:
   670→	; Inputs:
   671→	; XHL = ptr to STEP_1 or STEP_2
   672→	; XIX = p1
   673→	; XIY = p2

   675→	PUSHW 4000h		; uint16_t v = 0x4000;

   681→	SUB (DX), WA		; dx -= p1.x;
   682→
   683→	INC 2, XIX
   684→	INC 2, XIY
   685→	
   686→	LD WA, (XIY)
   687→	LD (POLYGON_H), WA		; dy = p2.y
   688→
   689→	LD WA, (XIX)
   690→	SUB (POLYGON_H), WA		; dy -= p1.y
   691→
   692→	CPW (POLYGON_H), 0
   693→	JP LE, POLYGON_H_IS_LE_ZERO  ; if (dy>0)

   695→	LD WA, (XSP)
   696→	EXTS XWA
   697→	LD DE, (POLYGON_H)
   698→	DIV XWA, DE

   706→	LD DE, (XSP)		; v
   707→	MULS XWA, DE
   708→	SLA 2, XWA
   709→	LD (XHL), XWA		; return dx * v * 4
   710→
   711→	INC 2, XSP

   715→readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy:
   716→	LD D, 0
   717→	LD E, C ; zoom
   718→	;	pt.x -= m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   719→	LD WA, 0
   720→	LD A, (XIX)
   721→	INC XIX
   722→	LD HL, (XSP + 6)
   723→	MUL XWA, DE			; PT.X *= ZOOM
   724→	SRA 6, WA			; PT.X /= default_zoom (40h)
   725→	SUB HL, WA
   726→	LD (XSP + 6), HL
   727→
   728→	;	pt.y -= m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   729→	LD WA, 0
   730→	LD A, (XIX)
   731→	INC XIX
   732→	LD HL, (XSP + 4)
   733→	MUL XWA, DE			; PT.Y *= ZOOM
   734→	SRA 6, WA			; PT.Y /= default_zoom (40h)
   735→	SUB HL, WA
   736→	LD (XSP + 4), HL
   737→
   738→	ld B, 0
   739→	LD C, (XIX)		; num_children - 1
   740→	INC XIX
   741→	INC BC			; BC = num_children
   742→
   743→children_loop:
   744→	LD WA, (XIX); offset 
   745→	INC 2, XIX
   746→	EX W, A
   747→	PUSH WA
   748→	PUSHW (XSP + 8); po.x = pt.x
   749→	PUSHW (XSP + 8); po.y = pt.y
   750→
   751→	; po.x += m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   752→	LD WA, 0
   753→	LD A, (XIX)
   754→	INC XIX
   755→	LD HL, (XSP + 2)
   756→	MUL XWA, DE			; PO.X *= ZOOM
   757→	SRA 6, WA			; PO.X /= default_zoom (40h)
   758→	ADD HL, WA
   759→	LD (XSP + 2), HL
   760→	
   761→	; po.y += m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   762→	LD WA, 0
   763→	LD A, (XIX)
   764→	INC XIX
   765→	LD HL, (XSP)
   766→	MUL XWA, DE			; PO.Y *= ZOOM
   767→	SRA 6, WA			; PO.Y /= default_zoom (40h)
   768→	ADD HL, WA
   769→	LD (XSP), HL
   770→
   771→	PUSH DE			; save zoom
   772→	LD DE, 0FFh				; uint16_t color = 0xFF;
   773→	LD HL, (XSP + 6) ;offset
   774→	AND HL, 8000h
   775→	JP Z, OFFSET_BIT15_NOT_SET
   776→	LD DE, 0
   777→	LD E,(XIX)				; 	color = m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] & 0x7F;
   778→	AND E, 7Fh
   779→	INC 2, XIX				; 	m_data_offset++; //and waste a byte...
   780→OFFSET_BIT15_NOT_SET:
   781→
   782→	PUSH XIX			;	 uint16_t backup = m_data_offset;
   783→	LD XIX, 0
   784→	LD IX, (XSP + 0Ah) ;offset
   785→	SLA 1, IX		 ; m_data_offset = (offset & 0x7FFF) * 2;
   786→	ADD XIX, INTRO_VIDEO_1
   787→	
   788→	LD HL, DE
   789→	; here L is the computer new color
   790→	; and BC is the children loop counter
   791→
   792→	; BC needs to become color | zoom params and
   793→	; DE needs to become x param
   794→	; to the readAndDrawPolygon routine
   795→	
   796→	LD DE, (XSP + 4)	; restore zoom
   797→
   798→	PUSH BC
   799→	LD B, L		; color
   800→	LD C, E		; zoom
   801→	LD DE, (XSP + 0ah)		; PO.x
   802→	LD HL, (XSP + 08h)		; PO.y
   803→	; (color, zoom, po)
   804→	CALL readAndDrawPolygon
   805→	POP BC
   806→	POP XIX				; m_data_offset = backup;
   807→	POP DE		; restore zoom
   808→
   809→	INC 6, XSP ; local vars offset, po.x, po.y
   810→	DJNZ BC, children_loop
   811→	RET

; (c) 2024 Felipe Correa da Silva Sanches <juca@members.fsf.org>
; Licensed under GPL version 2 or later.
;
; This is a port of the Another World VM (initially supporting only non-interactive
; playback of the game intro) to run from an extension board on a
; Technics SX-KN5000 musical keyboard.
;
; This program must replace the hd-ae5000_v2_01i.ic4 ROM of the extension board.
;
; This implementation is derived from my port of the Another World VM
; as a high-level emulation on MAME
;
; And that port was derived from Fabien Sanglard's AW-VM available at:
; https://github.com/fabiensanglard/Another-World-Bytecode-Interpreter
;
; The assembler I am using is compiled from source-code downloaded from
; http://john.ccac.rwth-aachen.de:8000/as/index.html
;
; Game assets must be extracted from an original copy of the game
; using the scripts provided at:
; https://github.com/felipesanches/AnotherWorld_VMTools
;
	cpu	96c141	; Actual CPU is 94c241f
	page	0
	maxmode	on

	ORG 0200000h

VM_VARIABLES:	DW	256 DUP (?)

THREADS_DATA:	DW	64*2 DUP (?)  ; For each of the 64 threads:
PC_OFFSET			EQU 0  ; 16 bits
REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET	EQU 2  ; 16 bits
INACTIVE_THREAD		EQU 0FFFFh
DELETE_THIS_THREAD	EQU 0FFFEh
NO_REQUEST 			EQU 0FFFFh

VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE:	DB	64*2 DUP (?)   ; For each of the 64 threads:
CURRENT_STATE	EQU 0  ; boolean stored as a byte
REQUESTED_STATE	EQU 1  ; boolean stored as a byte

FROZEN	EQU 0
NOT_FROZEN EQU 1
NO_STATE_REQUEST EQU 0FFh

CURRENT_THREAD: DB ?
PC:				DW ?
VM_STACK_POINTER: DD ?
VM_STACK: DW 256 DUP (?)

POLYGON_NUM_POINTS:	DB ?
POLYGON_BBOX_W:		DW ?					; uint16_t
POLYGON_BBOX_H:		DW ?					; uint16_t
POLYGON_POINTS:		DW	50 DUP (?, ?, ?)
POLYGON_XMIN:	DW ?						; int16_t
POLYGON_XMAX:	DW ?						; int16_t
POLYGON_YMIN:	DW ?						; int16_t
POLYGON_YMAX:	DW ?						; int16_t
HLINEY:		DW ?							; int16_t
CUR_LINE:			; uint32_t
CUR_LINE_LOW:	DW ?
CUR_LINE_HIGH:	DW ?

CPT1:				; uint32_t
CPT1_LOW:	DW ?
CPT1_HIGH:	DW ?

CPT2:				; uint32_t
CPT2_LOW:	DW ?
CPT2_HIGH:	DW ?

STEP1:				; int32_t
STEP1_LOW:	DW ?
STEP1_HIGH:	DW ?

STEP2:				; int32_t
STEP2_LOW:	DW ?
STEP2_HIGH:	DW ?

; int16_t x1, x2;
X1:			DW ?
X2:			DW ?

; 	uint16_t h;
POLYGON_H:	DW ?
DX:			DW ?	; int16_t

;	int16_t xmax, xmin
LINE_XMIN:	DW ?
LINE_XMAX:	DW ?
CUR_PAGE_PTR_1: DD ?
CUR_PAGE_PTR_2: DD ?
CUR_PAGE_PTR_3: DD ?

CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN:
	; int16_t xmax = MAX(x1, x2);
	LD WA, (X1)
	CP WA, (X2)
	JP GT, XMAX_OK
	LD WA, (X2)
XMAX_OK:
	LD (LINE_XMAX), WA
	
	; int16_t xmin = MIN(x1, x2);
	LD WA, (X1)
	CP WA, (X2)
	JP LT, XMIN_OK
	LD WA, (X2)
XMIN_OK:
	LD (LINE_XMIN), WA
	RET

drawLineN:
	; Inputs:
	; C = color
	PUSH XIX
	PUSH XHL
	
	CALL CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN

	; for (int16_t x=xmin; x<=xmax; x++)
	; 	m_curPagePtr1->pix(m_hliney, x) = color;
	LD XIX, (CUR_LINE)
	ADDW (CUR_LINE_LOW), 320
	ADCW (CUR_LINE_HIGH), 0
	LD HL, (LINE_XMIN)
	EXTS XHL
	ADD XIX, XHL
	LD HL, (LINE_XMAX)
	SUB HL, (LINE_XMIN)

drawLineN_loop:
	LDB (XIX), C
	INC XIX
	DJNZ HL, drawLineN_loop
	
	POP XHL
	POP XIX
	RET

drawPoint:
	PUSH XIX
	LD WA, 0
	LD WA, HL
	MUL XWA, 320
	; FIXME: do we need to zero the upper 16 bits of XDE here?
	ADD XWA, XDE
	LD XIX, 01a0000h
	ADD XIX, XWA
	LD (XIX), BC
	POP XIX
	RET

video MACRO type,data,x,y

	ENDM


text MACRO stringid, x, y, color
